# probmed

PR validation uses the [full local
gate](https://github.com/Data-Wise/probmed/blob/dev/tasks/PLAN-local-ci-transition-2026-10-20.md),
which posts a commit-specific required status after passing. GitHub
Actions still publishes the website on `main`; R-CMD-check remains
required on `main` PRs until branch protection is switched, while
coverage is manual.

**probmed** provides a robust framework for computing **$`P_{med}`$**, a
scale-free probabilistic effect size for causal mediation analysis.

## What is $`P_{med}`$?

$`P_{med}`$ offers an intuitive alternative to traditional mediation
effect sizes. With treatment held at its treated level $`x`$ for both
potential outcomes, it is the probability that the outcome when the
mediator takes its treated level $`M(x)`$ exceeds the outcome when it
takes its control level $`M(x^*)`$, with ties counted as one half:
$`P(Y(x, M(x)) > Y(x, M(x^*))) + \tfrac12 P(Y(x, M(x)) = Y(x, M(x^*)))`$.
The direct effect cancels, so $`P_{med}`$ is mediation-only.

Unlike the “Proportion Mediated” or simple indirect effect coefficients,
$`P_{med}`$: \* **Is Scale-Free**: Interpretable regardless of the units
of measurement for $`X`$, $`M`$, or $`Y`$. \* **Is Bounded**: Always
falls between 0 and 1, with 0.5 meaning no mediation effect, making it
comparable across studies. \* **Handles Non-Linearity**: Can be extended
to Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) where coefficients are not directly
comparable.

## Features

Single-mediator plug-in calls honor an explicit `seed`. MBCO is
deterministic and reports numerical statuses in `result@diagnostics`;
only verified likelihood-ratio endpoints set `converged = TRUE`, and
detected disconnected sets or failed profiles return missing interval
bounds. Parallel mediation keeps its legacy inversion path.

- **Flexible Modeling**: Gaussian (identity link) and binary (logit or
  probit link) mediators and outcomes, with covariates. Binary models
  are standardized over the observed covariate rows. Other families
  (Poisson, ordinal, …), interactions and transformed treatment/mediator
  terms are rejected with an informative error rather than simulated
  incorrectly.
- **Comprehensive Effect Reporting**: Provides both $`P_{med}`$
  (probabilistic effect size) and the traditional Indirect Effect
  ($`a \times b`$) with bootstrap confidence intervals.
- **Robust Inference**: Implements multiple methods for constructing
  confidence intervals:
  - **Parametric Bootstrap**: Efficient and accurate for large samples
    with known distributions.
  - **Nonparametric Bootstrap**: Robust to distributional assumptions
    (resampling-based).
  - **Plug-in Estimator**: Fast point estimation.
  - **MBCO** (Gaussian): deterministic likelihood-ratio interval with
    verified endpoints. It never undercovers but is conservative near
    the double null, flagged by `@diagnostics$pmed$near_double_null`.
  - **Model-based bootstrap** (opt-in, `method = "model_bootstrap"`):
    refits both equations on data simulated from the fitted models, so
    residual scales are re-estimated too. Coverage varies by design; see
    `docs/reports/CALIBRATION-2026-10-14.md` in the repository.
- **Modern Architecture**: Built on the **S7** object-oriented system,
  ensuring type safety, stability, and easy extensibility.
- **Ecosystem Integration**: Works seamlessly with popular R packages:
  - **lavaan**: Extract from Structural Equation Models with FIML and
    robust estimators
  - **mediation**: Direct integration with
    [`mediate()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/mediation/man/mediate.html)
    objects
  - Standard **lm/glm**: Native support for regression models
- **User-Friendly Interface**: Designed to work with standard R
  `formula` interfaces and `data.frame` inputs.

## Modern estimands

Beyond the core
[`pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed.md),
the package ships cross-fitted, influence-function-based estimators,
each with its own S7 result class. See the [Modern estimands
article](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/articles/modern-estimands.html)
for details and caveats.

| Function | Result class | What it estimates |
|----|----|----|
| [`ward_residual()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/ward_residual.md) | `GaugePmedResult` | Gauge-calibrated P_med (residual over observed effect) with weak-identification gates |
| [`incr_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/incr_pmed.md), [`incr_sensitivity()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/incr_sensitivity.md) | `IncrPmedResult` | Incremental P_med and its per-delta tipping analysis |
| [`sobol_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/sobol_pmed.md) | `SobolPmedResult` | Sobol variance-scale P_med |
| [`wasserstein_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/wasserstein_pmed.md) | `WassersteinPmedResult` | Wasserstein proportion mediated |
| [`rg_flow_contrast()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/rg_flow_contrast.md) | `RgFlowResult` | Scale-indexed NIE/TE with cluster-robust inference |
| [`pmed_sensitivity()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed_sensitivity.md) | `PmedSensitivity` | Unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding (tipping point) |

## Status and known limitations

The development version is `0.3.0.9000`; a release is on hold pending
manuscript submission. For the binary Wasserstein proportion mediated,
estimation near an exactly zero mediation path is hard: the plug-in bias
is of order $`n^{-1/4}`$, none of the point estimators tested met the
frozen bias gate (\|bias\|/SD \< .10) there, and that gate was shown to
be infeasible for any estimator with values in \[0, 1\] in the
zero-direct and weak-direct cells at n = 500, and the Fieller interval
is the supported uncertainty statement. See the [boundary article
section](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/articles/modern-estimands.html#boundary-behavior)
and `docs/reports/REPORT-boundary-point-risk-2026-10-21.md`.

## Mediationverse Ecosystem

**probmed** is part of the **mediationverse** ecosystem for mediation
analysis in R:

| Package | Purpose | Role |
|----|----|----|
| [**medfit**](https://github.com/data-wise/medfit) | Model fitting, extraction, bootstrap | Foundation |
| **probmed** (this) | Probabilistic effect size (P_med) | Application |
| [**RMediation**](https://github.com/data-wise/rmediation) | Confidence intervals (DOP, MBCO) | Application |
| [**medrobust**](https://github.com/data-wise/medrobust) | Sensitivity analysis | Application |
| [**medsim**](https://github.com/data-wise/medsim) | Simulation infrastructure | Support |

See [Ecosystem
Coordination](https://github.com/data-wise/medfit/blob/main/planning/ECOSYSTEM.md)
for version compatibility and development guidelines.

## Installation

Install from the [Data-Wise
r-universe](https://data-wise.r-universe.dev) — no compiler needed, and
dependencies (e.g. `medfit`) resolve automatically:

``` r

install.packages("probmed", repos = "https://data-wise.r-universe.dev")
```

Or install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/data-wise/probmed):

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("data-wise/probmed")
```

## Quick Example

Here is a basic example showing how to simulate data and compute
$`P_{med}`$ using a parametric bootstrap approach.

### 1. Simulate Data

First, we generate a dataset with a continuous treatment ($`X`$),
mediator ($`M`$), and outcome ($`Y`$), along with a covariate ($`C`$).

``` r

library(probmed)

set.seed(123)
n <- 300
data <- data.frame(X = rnorm(n), C = rnorm(n))

# Mediator model: M ~ X + C
data$M <- 0.5 * data$X + 0.3 * data$C + rnorm(n)

# Outcome model: Y ~ M + X + C
data$Y <- 0.4 * data$M + 0.2 * data$X + 0.2 * data$C + rnorm(n)
```

### 2. Compute $`P_{med}`$

We use the
[`pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed.md)
function to estimate the effect size. We specify the models for the
outcome and mediator, and select the bootstrap method.

``` r

result <- pmed(
  Y ~ X + M + C,             # Outcome model formula
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,     # Mediator model formula
  data = data,
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap",
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = 42
)
```

### 3. View Results

The results object provides a clear summary of both $`P_{med}`$ and the
Indirect Effect with confidence intervals.

``` r

print(result)
#>
#> P_med: Probability of Mediated Shift
#> ====================================
#>
#> Estimate: 0.55
#> 95% CI: [0.53, 0.572]
#>
#> Indirect Effect (Product of Coefficients):
#> Estimate: 0.2
#> 95% CI: [0.129, 0.283]
#>
#> Inference: parametric_bootstrap
#> Bootstrap samples: 1000
#>
#> Treatment contrast: X = 1 vs. X* = 0
#>
#> Interpretation:
#>   P(Y(1, M(1)) > Y(1, M(0))) = 0.55
#>   P that the mediator shift (M(0) -> M(1)) leaves a random individual better off, holding X = 1.

summary(result)
```

**Interpretation**: - **$`P_{med}`$ = 0.55**: Holding treatment at
$`X = 1`$, there is a 55% probability that the outcome under the treated
mediator level exceeds the outcome under the control mediator level.
Since 0.50 represents “no mediation effect”, this indicates a modest
positive mediation effect. - **Indirect Effect = 0.2**: The traditional
product-of-coefficients indirect effect ($`a \times b`$) quantifies the
average change in outcome due to the mediated path.

## Workflow Options

`probmed` offers three workflow approaches to suit your needs:

### 1. Formula Interface (Recommended for Most Users)

Directly specify your models using R formulas:

``` r

result <- pmed(
  Y ~ X + M + C,             # Outcome model
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,     # Mediator model
  data = data,
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap"
)
```

### 2. Integration with lavaan (For SEM Users)

Extract from fitted Structural Equation Models with full support for
FIML, robust estimators, and standardized estimates:

``` r

library(lavaan)

# Define SEM model
model <- '
  M ~ a*X + C
  Y ~ b*M + cp*X + C
'

# Fit with FIML for missing data
fit <- sem(model, data = data, missing = "fiml")

# Extract and compute P_med
extract <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M")
result <- pmed(extract, method = "parametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 5000)
print(result)
```

### 3. Integration with mediation Package

Seamlessly work with objects from the `mediation` package:

``` r

library(mediation)

# Fit models
model_m <- lm(M ~ X + C, data = data)
model_y <- lm(Y ~ M + X + C, data = data)

# Run mediate
med_out <- mediate(model_m, model_y, treat = "X", mediator = "M", boot = TRUE)

# Compute P_med from mediate object
result <- pmed(extract_mediation(med_out))
print(result)
```

## Advanced Features

### Generalized Linear Models (GLMs)

`probmed` supports GLMs for non-normal outcomes. For example, with a
binary outcome:

``` r

# Binary outcome example
data_bin <- data
data_bin$Y_binary <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.4 * data$M + 0.2 * data$X))

result_bin <- pmed(
  Y_binary ~ X + M + C,
  formula_m = M ~ X + C,
  data = data_bin,
  family_y = binomial(),    # Logistic regression for binary outcome
  treatment = "X",
  mediator = "M",
  method = "parametric_bootstrap",
  n_boot = 1000
)
print(result_bin)
```

### Bootstrap Methods Comparison

**When to use each method:**

- **Plugin** (`method = "plugin"`): Fast point estimates only, no
  confidence intervals. Use for quick exploration.
- **Parametric Bootstrap** (`method = "parametric_bootstrap"`): Default
  choice. Fast and accurate when parameter estimates are approximately
  normally distributed.
- **Nonparametric Bootstrap** (`method = "nonparametric_bootstrap"`):
  More robust to distributional assumptions but computationally
  intensive. Use when parametric assumptions are questionable.
- **MBCO** (`method = "mbco"`): Gaussian models only. Deterministic
  likelihood-ratio interval; check `result@diagnostics` for endpoint
  status.
- **Model-based bootstrap** (`method = "model_bootstrap"`, opt-in):
  simulates complete datasets from the fitted models with the observed
  treatment and covariates fixed, refits both equations, and reports the
  percentile interval only when at least 99% of draws are valid. Its
  coverage has not yet been calibrated.

``` r

# Compare methods
result_plugin <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                      treatment = "X", mediator = "M", method = "plugin")

result_param <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                     treatment = "X", mediator = "M",
                     method = "parametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 1000)

result_nonparam <- pmed(Y ~ X + M, formula_m = M ~ X, data = data,
                        treatment = "X", mediator = "M",
                        method = "nonparametric_bootstrap", n_boot = 1000)
```

# Package index

## Core Functions

Primary functions for computing P_med and extracting mediation
structures from fitted statistical models.

- [`pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed.md)
  : Compute P_med: Probabilistic Effect Size for Mediation
- [`pmed-formula`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed-formula.md)
  : Compute P_med from Formula
- [`pmed-MediationData`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed-MediationData.md)
  : Compute P_med from MediationData
- [`extract_mediation`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/extract_mediation.md)
  : Re-export extract_mediation from medfit

## Modern estimands

Cross-fitted, influence-function-based estimators beyond the core P_med:
the gauge residual (W = R/OE, with weak-identification gates),
incremental P_med, the Sobol variance-scale and Wasserstein versions,
and the scale-indexed rg-flow proportion mediated with cluster-robust
inference.

- [`ward_residual()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/ward_residual.md)
  : Gauge-Calibrated Proportion Mediated

- [`incr_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/incr_pmed.md)
  : Incremental Mediated Elasticity Curve

- [`incr_sensitivity()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/incr_sensitivity.md)
  : M–Y Confounding Sensitivity for the Incremental Mediated Elasticity

- [`sobol_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/sobol_pmed.md)
  : Sobol / Variance-Scale Proportion Mediated

- [`sobol_from_theta()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/sobol_from_theta.md)
  : Map corner means to the Sobol variance decomposition

- [`wasserstein_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/wasserstein_pmed.md)
  : Wasserstein / Transport-Scale Proportion Mediated

- [`pmedW_dr()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmedW_dr.md)
  : Doubly-Robust Wasserstein Proportion Mediated

- [`pmedW_md()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmedW_md.md)
  : Multivariate Wasserstein Proportion Mediated

- [`sinkhorn_div()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/sinkhorn_div.md)
  : Debiased Sinkhorn Divergence

- [`rg_flow_contrast()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/rg_flow_contrast.md)
  : Paired contrast of the proportion mediated between two scales

- [`rg_coarse_grain()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/rg_coarse_grain.md)
  :

  Coarse-grain multilevel data to aggregation scale `m`

- [`g_hat_eif()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/g_hat_eif.md)
  : Efficient-influence-function estimator of the scale-indexed
  proportion mediated

## Sensitivity analysis

Unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding: tipping-point analysis shared
across the estimands.

- [`pmed_sensitivity()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/pmed_sensitivity.md)
  : M–Y Confounding Sensitivity for a Proportion-Mediated Estimand

## S7 Class Definitions

Formal class structures for mediation analysis objects. These classes
define the object-oriented architecture of the package.

- [`PmedResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/PmedResult.md)
  : P_med Result Class
- [`GaugePmedResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/GaugePmedResult.md)
  : Gauge-Calibrated Proportion Mediated Result
- [`IncrPmedResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/IncrPmedResult.md)
  : Incremental Mediated Elasticity Result
- [`SobolPmedResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/SobolPmedResult.md)
  : Sobol / Variance-Scale Proportion Mediated Result
- [`WassersteinPmedResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/WassersteinPmedResult.md)
  : Wasserstein / Transport-Scale Proportion Mediated Result
- [`RgFlowResult()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/RgFlowResult.md)
  : Renormalization-Group Flow of the Proportion Mediated
- [`PmedSensitivity()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/PmedSensitivity.md)
  : P_med Sensitivity Result (M–Y Confounding)

  : Describe a family for an error message

- [`.is_gaussian()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-is_gaussian.md)
  : Is a family Gaussian (NULL is treated as Gaussian)?

- [`.label_vars()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-label_vars.md)
  : Data variables a model-matrix column label refers to

- [`.mbco_branch_lr()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_branch_lr.md)
  : Branch likelihood-ratio statistics for H0: a = 0 and H0: b = 0

- [`.mbco_fit_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_fit_pmed.md)
  : Signed Gaussian P_med profile with positive variance coordinates

- [`.mbco_gll()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_gll.md)
  : Gaussian profile log-likelihood given SSE, variance V, and n rows.

- [`.mbco_invert()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_invert.md)
  : Invert an LR test: find where excess(t) = LR(t) - crit crosses zero.

- [`.mbco_invert_verified()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_invert_verified.md)
  : Verified bounded-resolution LR inversion for single-mediator models

- [`.mbco_ll_constrained_ie()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_ll_constrained_ie.md)
  :

  Maximized log-likelihood under the constraint `a*b` = ie0

- [`.mbco_ll_constrained_ie_parallel()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_ll_constrained_ie_parallel.md)
  : Maximized log-likelihood under the constraint sum(a\*b) = ie0
  (parallel).

- [`.mbco_ll_constrained_pmed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_ll_constrained_pmed.md)
  : Maximized log-likelihood under the constraint P_med = pnorm(qstar).

- [`.mbco_ll_constrained_pmed_parallel()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_ll_constrained_pmed_parallel.md)
  : Maximized log-likelihood under the constraint joint P_med =
  pnorm(qstar).

- [`.mbco_ll_null()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_ll_null.md)
  : Gaussian exact-null union likelihood

- [`.mbco_lr_at()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_lr_at.md)
  : Profile LR statistic for H0: P_med = p (single-mediator Gaussian
  MBCO)

- [`.mbco_nlopt()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_nlopt.md)
  :

  One nloptr run in the [`optim()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/optim.html)
  result shape

- [`.mbco_optim()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_optim.md)
  : Convergence-checked nloptr minimizer with one deterministic fallback

- [`.mbco_parallel_ll()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_parallel_ll.md)
  : Joint Gaussian log-likelihood for the parallel free model at given
  params.

- [`.mbco_parallel_optim_best()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_parallel_optim_best.md)
  :

  Run Nelder-Mead from several starts, returning the best maximized
  log-likelihood (`-min value`), or NA if every start fails / is
  penalized.

- [`.mbco_parallel_starts()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_parallel_starts.md)
  : Deterministic perturbed warm starts for the parallel MBCO
  optimizers.

- [`.mbco_prep()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_prep.md)
  : Build design matrices and free-fit summaries for the MBCO
  optimization.

- [`.mbco_prep_parallel()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_prep_parallel.md)
  : Build design matrices and free-fit summaries for the parallel MBCO
  fit.

- [`.mbco_quadratic()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_quadratic.md)
  : Cached quadratic residual sum of squares for fixed nuisance designs

- [`.mbco_sse()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-mbco_sse.md)
  : Evaluate a precomputed residual quadratic

- [`.named_or()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-named_or.md)
  : Look up a named coefficient, returning a default when absent

- [`.needs_standardization()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-needs_standardization.md)
  : Does this model need covariate standardization?

- [`.offending_terms()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-offending_terms.md)
  : Model terms that involve a variable other than as its own main
  effect

- [`.ols_sse()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-ols_sse.md)
  : Residual sum of squares of an OLS fit of y on design matrix D.

- [`.pmed_compute()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_compute.md)
  : Core P_med Computation Dispatcher

- [`.pmed_compute_parallel()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_compute_parallel.md)
  : Dispatch parallel (joint) P_med by inference method.

- [`.pmed_core_simple()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_core_simple.md)
  : Simple P_med Core Computation

- [`.pmed_mbco()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_mbco.md)
  : MBCO Confidence Interval for P_med (Gaussian single-mediator model)

- [`.pmed_model_boot()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_model_boot.md)
  : Model-based response bootstrap for P_med (opt-in)

- [`.pmed_nonparametric_boot()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_nonparametric_boot.md)
  : Nonparametric Bootstrap for P_med

- [`.pmed_parallel_boot_result()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_boot_result.md)
  :

  Assemble a bootstrap `PmedResult` (shared by both parallel
  bootstraps).

- [`.pmed_parallel_closed()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_closed.md)
  : Closed-form joint P_med for parallel mediators (Gaussian).

- [`.pmed_parallel_coef_names()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_coef_names.md)
  :

  Names of the structural coefficients (a_j, b_j) in the parallel
  estimates vector / vcov. Uses the structural aliases `a{j}` / `b{j}`,
  which BOTH the lm/glm and lavaan medfit extractors expose (with full
  vcov rows) – unlike the source-specific `m{j}_<tx>` / `y_<mediator_j>`
  names, which exist only in the lm/glm extractor and would break the
  parametric bootstrap on a lavaan extract.

- [`.pmed_parallel_mbco()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_mbco.md)
  : MBCO confidence interval for parallel joint P_med (Gaussian).

- [`.pmed_parallel_nonparametric_boot()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_nonparametric_boot.md)
  : Nonparametric bootstrap for parallel joint P_med.

- [`.pmed_parallel_parametric_boot()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_parametric_boot.md)
  : Parametric bootstrap for parallel joint P_med.

- [`.pmed_parallel_plugin()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_plugin.md)
  : Plugin (point estimate only) for parallel joint P_med.

- [`.pmed_parallel_require_gaussian()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parallel_require_gaussian.md)
  : Require a Gaussian parallel extract (finite residual SDs present).

- [`.pmed_parametric_boot()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_parametric_boot.md)
  : Parametric Bootstrap for P_med

- [`.pmed_plugin()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-pmed_plugin.md)
  : Plugin Estimator (Point Estimate Only)

- [`.qr_sse()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-qr_sse.md)
  : Residual sum of squares against a precomputed QR decomposition.

- [`.split_coefs()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-split_coefs.md)
  : Split a joint coefficient vector into mediator and outcome parts

- [`.std_for()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-std_for.md)
  : Standardization inputs for one coefficient vector, or NULLs if not
  needed

- [`.std_linear_predictors()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-std_linear_predictors.md)
  : Per-row covariate linear predictors at x = 0 and m = 0

- [`.supported_family()`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/dot-supported_family.md)
  : Is a (family, link) pair one the core can simulate?

- [`lm_class`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/lm_class.md)
  : S3 Class Wrappers for S7

- [`` `%||%` ``](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/null-coalesce.md)
  : Null coalescing operator

- [`probmed-package`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/probmed-package.md)
  [`probmed`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/probmed-package.md)
  : probmed: Probabilistic Effect Sizes for Causal Mediation Analysis

- [`standardize`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/standardize.md)
  : Observed-sample covariate standardization

- [`support-guard`](https://data-wise.github.io/probmed/dev/reference/support-guard.md)
  : Supported-model guard for single-mediator P_med
